correctness.rationale: A Gaussian in the zero-sum subspace has uniform coordinate ordering; maximizing independent edge segments yields an orientation. Because missing edges form a matching, the only incomparable elements are consecutive deleted pairs, so each orientation class has exactly 2^s permutations. Binomial inversion counts exact s-layers and summing squared cone masses gives the collision identity. Local uniform convergence of the generating function follows from coefficient bound (2k/n)^t/t!<=1/t!, giving both Poisson limits and asymptotic constants. A standalone standard-library exact rational checker passed every k at n=2,...,8 (23 cases); the n=2 case is only boundary testing. Finite enumerations are corroboration, not the proof of the universal limits.

originality.rationale: The general normal fan, orientation classes and matching-deleted acyclic orientation total counts are established previously and credited. The exact all-k Gaussian angle multiplicities, squared-angle collision probability and distinct Poisson parameters for direction/vertex sampling are mathematically stronger data than these prior counts; no covering statement was found in the inspected primary claims, relevant published records or exact database entries. An unindexed equivalent refined orientation enumeration remains a bounded risk.
residual_risks: Refined adjacency-block enumerations or sampling-bias identities might have appeared in permutation, hyperplane-arrangement, or random-ranking literature under terminology not retrieved.

value.rationale: The exact Gaussian cone-angle census is a complete geometric observable for a natural infinite family of dense graphical zonotopes. The two different Poisson limits exhibit a genuine discrepancy between random supporting-direction and uniform-vertex sampling, quantified by the sharp nontrivial factor e^rho for collision above the uniform baseline. These stochastic-geometric data are not determined by the already-known aggregate vertex count. The full-angle classification and scaling limit, rather than a small reparametrization or isolated finite table entry, motivate the precise invariant.
